extra_misconceptions.fact: Paleontologists study non-avian dinosaurs, which went extinct millions of years before humans and their material culture existed.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Archaeologists excavate dinosaur skeletons and study ancient reptiles alongside early human stone tools.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Archaeologists prioritize recording context and spatial data to reconstruct human behavior rather than selling objects for profit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Treasure hunters and archaeologists share the same goals because both recover rare objects from buried ruins.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Historians rely primarily on written records, whereas archaeologists analyze physical remains from both literate and preliterate eras.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: History and archaeology examine identical evidence by reading written manuscripts and royal decrees from ancient cities.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Archaeology is one of the four main subfields of anthropology, alongside cultural, biological, and linguistic anthropology.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Anthropology is a narrow subdiscipline of archaeology that only studies living tribal communities in remote regions.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the scientific value of a projectile point when a collector pulls it from the soil without logging context?
Which physical indicator in an exposed rock layer distinguishes an archaeological hearth from a paleontological fossil bed?
Under what condition does an archaeologist collaborate directly with a geologist during a prehistoric site excavation?
What field measurement confirms the exact three-dimensional provenience of an artifact before it is lifted from its matrix?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Archival research, survey design, and post-excavation laboratory analysis require far more time than actual digging in the field.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Field excavation is the first step in an archaeological project and takes up most of the research schedule.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excavation destroys a site as it proceeds, so archaeologists leave unexcavated areas intact for future researchers with better tools.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Archaeologists excavate an entire site completely so that no buried features or artifacts are left behind.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Washing pottery carelessly removes microscopic food residues, pollen, and pigments needed for chemical and botanical analysis.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scrubbing every excavated potsherd clean in the field makes laboratory cataloging faster and more accurate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ethical standards require publishing findings and archiving field notes so the public and scientific community can verify results.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Keeping site reports unpublished protects the intellectual property of the lead archaeologist indefinitely.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to begin digging test units at a site before completing a formal research design and curation plan?
What happens to fragile organic artifacts if they are washed with water immediately after removal from dry soil?
Which surface survey method allows a field crew to detect buried walls and ditches without disturbing a single spade of dirt?
Where should a field technician record soil color and texture changes before bagging artifacts from a newly excavated level?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Carbon-14 dating works only on once-living organic matter such as charcoal, bone, shell, wood, or charred plant seeds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Radiocarbon dating measures the exact calendar age of stone tools, bronze weapons, and fired clay vessels directly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Relative dating establishes only whether one layer or artifact is older or younger than another without assigning a calendar year.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Relative dating techniques provide a calendar date range with a statistical margin of error measured in years.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Trash pits, burials, erosion, and animal burrows frequently mix soil layers and move older objects above younger deposits.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Deeper artifacts in an excavation unit are always older than objects recovered closer to the modern ground surface.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tree-ring dating requires species with distinct annual growth rings and a continuous regional master sequence for comparison.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dendrochronology works on any piece of burnt firewood regardless of tree species or geographic region.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does rodent burrowing or frost heave invalidate the Law of Superposition within a test pit?
Which physical indicator in a wooden roof beam allows a dendrochronologist to determine the exact year the tree was felled?
Why is it impossible to date a quartz arrowhead or a granite grinding stone directly using radiocarbon analysis?
What happens to the accuracy of a radiocarbon sample if modern rootlets or cigarette ash touch the charcoal during collection?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Domestic middens and common houses preserve everyday tools, food scraps, and broken pottery that reflect how most people lived.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Monumental stone pyramids and royal tombs tell archaeologists more about daily life than ordinary household trash middens.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sites like Cahokia and Pueblo Bonito show that Indigenous North Americans engineered urban centers, plazas, and complex earthen mounds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pre-Columbian societies in North America lived only in small nomadic bands and never built permanent cities.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE buried Pompeii in volcanic ash and pumice within hours, freezing daily Roman life in place.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pompeii was buried slowly over several centuries by windblown dust after its residents abandoned the Roman Empire.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sites are usually located through systematic pedestrian surveys, aerial photography, soil testing, and routine construction monitoring.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Most archaeological sites are discovered by explorers hacking through jungles in search of lost cities of gold.

extra_socratic_questions: Which environmental factor preserved wooden buildings and leather shoes at waterlogged sites while dry sites lost all organics?
What measurement confirms the layout of ancient Maya causeways and agricultural terraces hidden beneath dense jungle canopy?
Under what condition does an accidental construction discovery turn into a legally protected salvage excavation?
What physical evidence at Cahokia or Mesa Verde demonstrates long-distance trade networks across North America?

extra_misconceptions.fact: ARPA governs federal and Indian lands, whereas artifacts on private land fall under state burial statutes and property laws.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The Archaeological Resources Protection Act regulates artifact collecting on privately owned farmland across the United States.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Federal law prohibits disturbing or removing any archaeological or historic object from National Park lands without a research permit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Surface collecting arrowheads in a National Park is legal as long as the visitor does not use a shovel or metal detector.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Section 106 requires federal agencies to assess impacts on historic properties and mitigate harm before construction proceeds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act permanently blocks any federal construction project that hits an old site.

extra_misconceptions.fact: NAGPRA mandates that museums and federal agencies inventory and repatriate Native American human remains and sacred items to tribes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Museums may keep Indigenous human remains and funerary objects indefinitely if they were excavated before 1990.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act require halting a dig immediately?
What legal threshold under ARPA distinguishes a misdemeanor citation from a felony prosecution on federal public land?
Why does Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act apply to a private highway project that uses federal funds?
Which international convention restricts the import and export of looted antiquities across national borders?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Removing an artifact destroys its spatial association with nearby features; leave it in place, photograph it, and report the coordinates.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Picking up an exposed arrowhead on a public trail saves the artifact from erosion and helps local museum curators.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Skin oils and moisture accelerate mineral crusts, bacterial growth, and flaking that permanently destroy painted pictographs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Touching ancient rock art with bare hands or wetting it with water is a harmless way to make faded pigments show up in photos.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every past culture and site is unique and nonrenewable; once a site is looted or bulldozed, that chapter of history is lost forever.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Archaeological sites are a renewable cultural resource because modern society creates new trash and buildings every day.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Broadcasting exact coordinates attracts looters and heavy foot traffic that erode fragile walls; share locations only with land managers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Posting exact GPS pins of backcountry cliff dwellings on social media promotes public appreciation and site safety.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the charcoal layers inside a rock shelter when campers build a modern fire ring directly on the cave floor?
Where should a Scout record GPS coordinates and place a scale object when photographing an exposed artifact on a trail?
Why is it dangerous to make chalk outlines or latex molds directly on prehistoric petroglyphs and painted pictographs?
Which agency official should a hiker notify after spotting an eroded burial or pottery cluster on state forest land?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Compacted landfills lack oxygen and moisture, mummifying paper, food waste, and plastics for decades as shown by garbology studies.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern landfills decompose rapidly into dark soil because moisture and bacteria break down buried household garbage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: People routinely underreport junk food and waste in interviews, making physical trash analysis a more accurate measure of consumption.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Household surveys of eating habits always match the physical evidence found in a family's weekly garbage bin.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Museums exhibit only a small fraction of their holdings while preserving the rest in climate-controlled collections for scientific study.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Museum curators display every artifact recovered from an excavation in public glass cases for visitors to inspect.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Without written provenance linking an heirloom to specific people, dates, and places, its personal context vanishes within a generation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An unlabeled family heirloom holds the same historical value whether or not relatives write down its oral history.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator on a family heirloom reveals how it was repaired or repurposed across multiple generations?
What happens to a future archaeologist's view of your household diet if all compostable food scraps decay before excavation?
Why is a museum exhibit label incomplete if it shows a bronze tool without explaining who used it and where it was found?
What pattern in a one-week household trash log distinguishes weekday convenience meals from weekend family gatherings?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rotted wooden posts leave distinct dark circular soil stains called postmolds that preserve the exact floor plan of ancient buildings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wooden houses and log cabins rot away completely and leave zero physical trace in the soil for archaeologists to detect.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plant foods decay faster than bone and stone, so archaeologists use flotation and pollen analysis to recover charred seeds and grains.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Finding stone projectile points at a camp proves that the inhabitants ate only large mammals and gathered no wild plants.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Written records often omit marginalized groups, laborers, and Indigenous communities whose daily lives are preserved in site artifacts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Historical maps and county histories record the daily lives of all regional inhabitants over a century ago without bias.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Non-local raw materials usually moved across regions through down-the-line trade networks connecting many neighboring communities.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Exotic materials like marine shells or copper found far inland prove that the local inhabitants traveled to the coast themselves.

extra_socratic_questions: Which soil stain pattern allows an archaeologist to reconstruct the footprint of a wooden house after the logs have rotted away?
What physical evidence in a regional hearth reveals whether past inhabitants ate wild game, farmed crops, or imported foods?
Why do stone tools, glass beads, and fired ceramics survive in local soils long after woven baskets and hide clothing vanish?
What measurement confirms that obsidian flakes or marine shells at an inland site arrived through long-distance trade networks?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over eighty percent of U.S. archaeologists work in Cultural Resource Management, surveying construction sites for Section 106 compliance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Most professional archaeologists work for universities and spend their careers excavating overseas temples and royal tombs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Directing federal archaeological permits requires a master's degree or doctorate plus months of supervised field experience.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-year bachelor's degree in anthropology qualifies a graduate to direct federal archaeological excavations independently.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Beginning field technicians often work seasonal, project-by-project contracts where hourly wages and per diem rates vary by region.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Entry-level archaeological field technicians earn salaried year-round income with paid travel between regional excavation sites.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Employers require an accredited multi-week archaeological field school where students practice stratigraphy, mapping, and excavation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Classroom coursework alone satisfies hiring requirements for entry-level Cultural Resource Management survey and lab positions.

extra_socratic_questions: What Youth Protection steps must a Scout complete before conducting an informational interview with a practicing archaeologist?
Which degree and field school credentials separate a Principal Investigator from an entry-level shovelbum technician?
What expenses beyond university tuition must your career research log include when pricing an accredited field school?
Under what condition does a commercial field archaeologist require OSHA trench safety training before entering a deep test unit?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Artifacts must remain in situ until three-dimensional datum coordinates, soil associations, and photographs are logged in the unit record.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling an exposed projectile point out of a unit floor right away protects the fragile stone from being stepped on during digging.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Abrasive brushing destroys fugitive paint, microscopic tool marks, and organic residues needed for radiocarbon or starch grain analysis.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scrubbing newly excavated pottery sherds and bone with a stiff wire brush removes hardened clay faster in the field laboratory.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ground surfaces slope and erode unevenly, so all vertical depths must be measured from a fixed horizontal datum string with a line level.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Measuring artifact depth from the modern ground surface above the corner stake gives an accurate vertical elevation across a unit.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Lithic debitage and fire-cracked rock reveal toolmaking workshops and hearth locations, so all cultural material is collected by level.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Discarding unworked fire-cracked rock and tiny chert flakes from the shaker screen keeps specimen bags focused on diagnostic tools.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to an artifact's scientific context if it is bagged before the unit and stratum level tag is filled out?
Which physical indicator in a test unit wall tells an excavator to switch from arbitrary ten-centimeter levels to natural strata?
What measurement confirms that a string and line level are horizontal before recording an artifact's depth below the unit datum?
Why is it dangerous to undercut a deep excavation balk wall or stack heavy spoil buckets directly along the edge of a test pit?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Experimental replication shows only that a method is plausible and must be verified by matching microwear traces on original artifacts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Building a working replica with authentic stone tools proves that ancient people manufactured the original artifact the exact same way.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Museum exhibits conceal exact site coordinates under the Archaeological Resources Protection Act to prevent looting and vandalism.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Public exhibit maps should print exact GPS coordinates of excavation sites so museum visitors can hike out and view the ruins.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High light intensity and heat break down organic fibers and collagen, so museum cases use low-lux LED lighting and UV filters.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mounting genuine prehistoric textiles and bone needles under bright halogen spotlights helps visitors see fine weaving details clearly.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Conservation ethics require reversible archival adhesives like Paraloid B-72 so future researchers can safely disassemble the vessel.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Gluing broken pottery sherds together with household cyanoacrylate superglue creates a permanent bond for a school display case.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the validity of an experimental archaeology test if you use modern steel tools to shape a prehistoric bow stave?
Which detail must be omitted from a public museum exhibit label to protect an active archaeological site from illegal looting?
What measurement confirms that a museum display case maintains safe light and relative humidity levels for organic basketry?
Why is it dangerous to percussion-flake obsidian or chert without impact safety glasses, leather pads, and outdoor ventilation?
